name: Schloss Matzen
kurzbeschreibung: Picturesque castle near Reith in the Alpbachtal, surrounded by the heritage-listed 15-hectare Matzen Park with tranquil ponds and exotic trees.
preis: Schlosspark frei zugänglich, Schloss beherbergt Hotel und Restaurant
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Oktober, Führungen nach Vereinbarung
beschreibung:
Überblick

Historic Schloss Matzen stands picturesquely on a gentle hill at the entrance to the Alpbachtal valley near Reith and Brixlegg. First documented in the 12th century, the fortified stronghold with its prominent round keep guarded the river crossings of the Inn. In the late 19th century, Irish peer Baron Groote transformed the estate into a romantic neo-Gothic residence. Today, the castle houses a boutique luxury hotel. The main highlight for the public is the adjacent 15-hectare Matzen Park, legally protected as one of Tyrol's most valuable historical landscaped gardens.

Route & Anforderungen

A network of level, well-kept gravel walking paths weaves through Matzen Park. Trails meander around the scenic Lion Pond and Carp Pond, crossing tree-shaded lawns and passing exotic trees over 150 years old, including giant sequoias, tulip trees, and ginkgos planted by 19th-century botanists. The paths are entirely flat, paved with smooth gravel, and barrier-free, making them ideal for families with pushchairs, wheelchair users, and dog walkers. Allow one to two hours to leisurely explore the park. Dogs are welcome on a leash.

Besuch & Anreise

Matzen Park is open free of charge year-round from dawn to dusk. By car, take the Inntal motorway A12 to the Kramsach/Alpbachtal exit, then follow signs toward Brixlegg and Reith im Alpbachtal. Free car parking is located right beside the main park entrance along Matzenstraße. Rail passengers can alight at Brixlegg railway station, followed by an easy 15-minute walk along signposted pathways to the park gates.

Tipps

After circling the tranquil ponds, stop for coffee or local cuisine on the terrace of Gut Matzen restaurant, enjoying splendid views of the castle keep and the Rofan mountains.
